evals.prompt: Harden the existing Maven Java 11 Mu Server 2.4.1 application in this directory without changing its dependency, package, port 8192, or /api/health contract. Keep the UI at /app, serve from src/main/resources/public while developing and the packaged /public classpath root otherwise. Allow only GET and HEAD on static paths; return 405 with Allow for POST. Disable directory listing. Give app.a1b2c3.js a one-year public immutable cache and keep index.html revalidatable, with nosniff on regular assets. Add an SPA fallback for extensionless /app navigation paths, but keep missing asset files and /api paths as 404. Build and test both source-directory and packaged working-directory launches, GET/HEAD/POST, the bare /app redirect, caching, a client route, a missing bundle, and API fall-through.
evals.expected_output: A scoped, ordered Mu Server static/SPA handler chain whose method, directory, cache, packaging, fallback, and 404 contracts are verified over HTTP in both file and classpath modes.
assertions: The project compiles on Java 11 and preserves io.muserver:mu-server 2.4.1, package example, port 8192, one server, and GET /api/health returning 200 with body healthy.

The /app context contains an application-owned method guard before ResourceHandler; GET and HEAD fall through, while POST /app/index.html returns 405 with Allow listing GET and HEAD and does not serve the file.

ResourceHandlerBuilder.fileOrClasspath retains the configured source and classpath roots, directory listing is disabled, /app redirects to /app/, and GET /app/ serves the exact index in both a project-root launch and a launch where the source path is absent.

GET and HEAD for app.a1b2c3.js have the correct JavaScript content type, nosniff, and a public one-year immutable cache policy; HEAD has no response body. index.html remains revalidatable rather than immutable.
An extensionless path such as /app/orders/42 returns the SPA index for GET/HEAD, while /app/missing.a1b2c3.js and /api/missing remain 404 and are not rewritten to HTML.
A request for /app/docs/ does not expose a directory listing or the internal-note.txt filename.
HTTP tests assert status, body bytes, Content-Type, Cache-Control, X-Content-Type-Options, Location, Allow, and fall-through rather than only compiling the configuration.

evals.prompt: Review our Mu Server static download handler and its tests. The team assumes ResourceHandler automatically rejects non-GET methods, emits ETags, implements If-Range, returns 416 for invalid ranges, and supports multipart ranges. Verify those claims against the selected Mu version, then update tests and any application-owned method policy. Cover GET/HEAD/POST, If-Modified-Since, a single prefix/suffix/open-ended range, multiple and unsatisfiable ranges, gzip negotiation, and custom cache/security headers without changing download bytes.
evals.expected_output: A source-backed correction of the assumed ResourceHandler contract, a scoped GET/HEAD policy where required, and wire-level tests for validators, ranges, compression, and metadata.
assertions: The review identifies the selected Mu Server major line and verifies behavior against implementation/tests rather than assuming generic static-server semantics.

It states that ResourceHandler itself can serve an existing resource for methods such as POST and that only HEAD suppresses the regular-file body; any 405/Allow behavior is implemented in an earlier application handler.
It records that Last-Modified and If-Modified-Since are supported, while ResourceHandler emits no ETag and does not process If-None-Match or If-Range.

It verifies one satisfiable range as 206 with exact Content-Range/body and records that multiple, malformed, and unsatisfiable ranges are ignored in favor of the full 200 response rather than 416 or multipart/byteranges.
It tests HEAD headers and empty body, invalid If-Modified-Since fall-through, and the interaction in which a matching If-Modified-Since produces 304 before Range processing.

It distinguishes ResourceType gzip eligibility from MuServerBuilder compression configuration, verifies Content-Encoding and Vary for negotiated gzip, and exercises range behavior with the intended Accept-Encoding policy.
Custom cache and security headers use ResourceCustomizer only for existing regular resources, preserve length/validator/range metadata, and are asserted over HTTP.

evals.prompt: Move our /docs static Swagger UI setup from Mu Server 2.4.1 to Mu Server 3. We currently depend on org.webjars:swagger-ui at a pinned version and mount classpathHandler('/META-INF/resources/webjars/swagger-ui/' + version). Show the appropriate Mu 3 ResourceHandlerBuilder API, decide whether explicit or metadata-discovered versioning is safer for our reproducible build, explain the supported metadata groups and failure cases, preserve io.muserver:mu-server coordinates, and test packaged startup plus the UI entry file. Also flag any static filename behavior around literal plus signs that needs an upgrade regression test.
evals.expected_output: A Mu Server 3 WebJar migration that preserves coordinates and dependency pinning, selects the correct WebJar overload with understood metadata behavior, and verifies packaged resource paths and relevant 2.x/3.x decoding differences.
assertions: The answer treats Mu Server 3 as released, retains io.muserver:mu-server, and does not use io.muserver:mu3 or invent a final 3.x artifact number.

It uses webjarHandler('swagger-ui', version) for explicit deterministic selection or gives a justified one-argument choice; it explains that the WebJar remains an intentional org.webjars:swagger-ui runtime dependency.
It states that the two-argument overload maps to /META-INF/resources/webjars/swagger-ui/<version> and validates artifact/version as single path segments.

For one-argument discovery it identifies pom.properties under org.webjars and org.webjars.npm metadata, and describes missing metadata and multiple distinct versions as construction-time errors resolved by the explicit overload.
It explains that Mu 2.4.1's manual classpathHandler path remains the compatibility fallback and keeps the configured dependency version synchronized with the served path.
Packaged tests launch outside the source working directory and assert the actual UI entry filename, representative dependent assets, content types, caching, and 404 for a nonexistent resource.
The upgrade review tests filenames containing a literal plus, %2B, and spaces because 2.x form-style path decoding and 3.x URI path decoding differ.
